issues.detail: Missing error handling for edge cases such as password-protected PDFs, missing or uninstalled language packs, and completely unreadable scans.
Installation instructions provided only for Ubuntu/Debian and macOS; Windows users must install Tesseract and Poppler through alternative methods without documented guidance.

scenarios.name: multilingual-contract-ocr
scenarios.rationale: Response A fully covers all three rubric requirements: correct language syntax (`lang='eng+fra'`), platform-specific installation with verification via `tesseract --list-langs`, and comprehensive confidence score extraction and reporting. Response B covers only the language syntax correctly, provides partial installation instructions without showing how to verify language packs are installed, omits confidence scoring entirely, and ends by asking for clarification rather than delivering a complete answer.

scenarios.name: batch-receipt-processing-with-quality-flags
scenarios.rationale: Response A delivers complete, production-ready code that covers all three rubric requirements: checks for existing text layers with pdfplumber before processing, reports per-file and per-page confidence scores, and flags files with <85% confidence for manual review with specific page numbers; Response B asks clarifying questions but provides zero implementation of any required functionality.

scenarios.name: degraded-scan-text-extraction
scenarios.rationale: Response A directly addresses all four rubric requirements: specifies 400 DPI, implements contrast/sharpening preprocessing, reports per-page confidence scores with averaging, and identifies low-confidence words (< 70%) with detailed flagging. Response B fails to meet any rubric requirement—it requests the file rather than providing the DPI specification, preprocessing method, confidence reporting, or unreliable-section identification the task asks for.
